candidates.summary: The variadic spread f(s...) still checks element assignability, not identity: []int passes as ...any and []E as ...error, so the callee can write a string into the caller's []int
candidates.failure_scenario: func f(xs ...any) { xs[0] = "hello" }; s := []int{1, 2}; f(s...); println(s[0]) prints `hello`: an []int element holds a string. g([]E{{}, {}}...) with g(xs ...error) is accepted too. Go rejects both calls at compile time ('cannot use s (variable of type []int) as []any value'). The SliceType cdt.Vrd branch, `return checkAssignableTo(n, st.Elt, cdt.Elt)`, is the same element-assignability recursion this PR removes from the *PointerType case (the ADR names it: 'recursed into assignability, which accepted interface targets'), and the PR body says slice elements now use exact identity. The line predates the diff; it is in scope because the diff sweeps this class and misses this member. On chain the keeper's go/types pass rejects the deploy; `gno run` does not run that pass, and the probe ran there.

candidates.summary: The PR body lists copy_struct_tags.gno as a static rejection, but the VM accepts copy() between slices whose element types differ: the test pins only the go/types error, and copy([]int, []string) stores a string in an []int
candidates.failure_scenario: The builtin declares dst and src as two independent generics (uverse.go:858-859, GenT("X") and GenT("Y")), so specifyType never compares their element types and the identity change in specifyType never reaches copy. copy_struct_tags.gno carries only `// TypeCheckError:` and no `// Error:` line (it is the only one of the PR's 11 'static rejection' filetests with none), so its PASS means the VM ran the copy. The same shape with unrelated element types: dst := make([]int, 1); copy(dst, []string{"x"}); println(dst[0]) prints `x`, so an int-typed slot holds a string. The ADR's 'uverse generic unification uses exact identity' and the PR body's 'static rejections (... copy_struct_tags)' do not hold for the VM. The copy builtin predates the diff; it is in scope because the diff adds a test that pins the VM's acceptance and presents it as a rejection. On chain the keeper's go/types pass rejects the deploy.
